text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS TIMES
- The federal government has directed that a uniform import duty of 25 percent will be charged on imported four wheel drive vehicles.
- Financial reports of oil marketing firms shows that they are being weighed down by trade debts.
- Nigerian stock exchange seals off against external access the computer terminals of its recently launched clearing system to check activities of fraudsters.
- Fuel supply situation in Lagos area may not improve soon.
- Cement makers in Nigeria have bowed to the ban on import of gypsum as the raw material has been found in the country.
DAILY TIMES
- Minister of state for agriculture Professor Ademola Adesina dies at 54 of asthma attack.
- As part of efforts to sanitise national carrier, management of Nigeria Airways has decided to close all unviable local and foreign offices beginning with New York.
- Banks and others investing in government debt instruments have continued to shun treasury bills because of the low level of liquidity in the financial system.
THE GUARDIAN
- Fresh crisis in oil town of Warri, 18 houses burnt and some people feared dead as Ijaw and Itsekiri youth clash again.
- Nigeria, seven others create economic and trading co-operation body of developing countries known as D-8 in Istanbul, Turkey.
- Financial autonomy is coming for Nigeria's judiciary.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani restates government interest in privatisation at a lecture in the northern city of Kaduna.
- ING Barings of The Netherlands raises $30 million syndicated loan facility for Nigerian oil firm Amni International Petroleum Development Company.
THISDAY

- There are indications that some European countries may try to stop Nigeria from taking part in next year's World Cup soccer tournament in France because of a European Union sporting ban on Nigeria over human rights and lack of democracy.
